# Substitutes

> "Flee from youthful lusts; but pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart."
>
> — 2 Timothy 2:22

When a man stops, he looks round for something to put in the gap. The usual candidates are:

- **Edging.** Going right up to the line and stopping short, so that "technically" nothing happened.
- **"Just touching."** A hand under the covers that isn't *doing* anything.
- **Porn "instead".** Looking without touching, as if the eyes were a separate department.
- **The endless scroll.** Reels, thirst traps, the Explore page, the "accidental" search.
- **Food.** The fridge at midnight.

USE NONE OF THEM.

Substitutes don't make it easier. They make it harder. If an urge comes and you answer it with a substitute, you haven't ended the urge. You've stretched it out. And you've told yourself something fatal: "There's a hole here, and I need to stuff it with something." That's handing the screaming toddler the sweets. You get five minutes of quiet and the same scene again tomorrow.

Three things to remember:

1. **There is no substitute for masturbation,** because nothing is missing.
2. **You don't need it.** It was never food. When an urge comes, remind yourself that men in the trap have urges all the time and free men don't. The urge is one more thing the habit did to you, and what you're feeling is the Little Monster dying.
3. **The habit made the void. It never filled it.** The sooner you show your body and mind that there's nothing to fill, the sooner you're free.

## The near-beer of lust {-}

The first four on the list aren't substitutes at all. They're the same drug in a smaller glass.

Start with edging. A recovery site defines it as "masturbating up to the edge of orgasm, then stopping to cool things down, then revving up again." The man who does it thinks he's kept his vow on a technicality. In fact he has spent an hour doing exactly what he swore off, and fed the Little Monster a banquet.

"Just touching" is edging that hasn't admitted it yet.

Porn "instead" is the worst trade of the lot. If you came here from EasyPeasy, you climbed out of that pit once. Don't go back in because you've decided the hand was the only problem.

Then there's the scroll, the modern favourite. He isn't *looking at porn*. He's looking at a fitness account, then a beach reel, then whatever the algorithm has learned he'll stop for. One coach is blunt about what those feeds are for: "they come up with new trends every month". They're built to keep you simmering. A man who scrolls thirst traps and doesn't touch himself has not stopped. He's a man on a diet who spends his evenings standing in the bakery. Jesus's words about the look in Matthew 5:28 still apply to him.

Heath Lambert described the whole family in one line: "Lust never has what it wants because it never has enough." That's why none of these can satisfy you. They are lust in a smaller dose.

## Why substitutes sound so sensible {-}

If you don't understand the trap, a softer version sounds perfectly logical. The thinking goes that a quitter has two big enemies:

1. the habit itself, and
2. a terrible period of physical withdrawal.

With two big enemies, you'd be wise not to fight both at once. So you wean yourself. First drop the porn but keep the hand. Then drop the finish but keep the touching. Then taper down gently until one day you wake up free.

It's very reasonable, and it's wrong, because both of its facts are wrong. The habit is not a mighty enemy. It's a trick, and you've seen how it's done. And there is no terrible withdrawal: the physical side is so slight that most men can't tell it from being a bit peckish. So you have one job, which is to starve the Little Monster and bury the Big Monster as quickly as possible. Every substitute on the list does the reverse. It keeps the little one fed, and that keeps the big one alive.

Ask yourself how any man could cure a craving by taking a little of what he craves. A few men do taper their way out, and they got free in spite of the taper. Many more end up in the tug-of-war from Chapter 11, straining against something they're still half holding on to, until giving in feels like a relief.

## The fridge {-}

Some men turn to food. The empty, restless feeling of the Little Monster is very like hunger, so they try to feed it. It doesn't work. A man who has stuffed himself and lies heavy and bored on the sofa is in just the state where the old thought comes most easily. You'd only swap one problem for two: you'd get fat and miserable, and be back at the habit within a month.

The real damage a substitute does isn't in your stomach or under the covers. It's in your head. Do you look for a substitute for the flu once it's cleared up? Of course not. When you say "I need something in its place", you're saying "I've made a sacrifice", and that one belief is what makes the Willpower Method so miserable. A man who goes looking for a replacement has told himself he lost something.

## "But it's my little reward" {-}

The lighter users find this hardest. The man who "only" did it after a hard week, or when the house was empty, thinks of it as a treat. "How will I unwind?" he says. That question gives him away. Mostly he didn't reach for it because he wanted to unwind. He reached for it because the Little Monster wanted feeding, and afterwards he called it unwinding.

Remember the tight shoes from Chapter 3. That's all your "reward" ever was: the relief of taking off something that pinched. So if you really must have a treat to replace it, here's one. Buy boots a size too small. Wear them all day and don't take them off till evening. Then enjoy that glorious moment when they come off.

You think that's ridiculous, and you're right. But that is exactly what you've been doing for years. Soon you won't need the "reward" at all, and you'll look at men who do with real pity.

## Pursue {-}

Look again at Paul's sentence to Timothy. He gives two instructions. The first is *flee*: don't negotiate with it or keep a milder version of it. The second is *pursue*: go after righteousness, faith, love and peace, and do it "with those who call on the Lord", which means in company.

That is not a substitute. A substitute is a thing you grab to plug a hole. Paul is describing a life you can now get on with. You'll have evenings and energy to spare. Spend them on things that are good in themselves.

One man put his whole story in a blog comment: "I Quit Masturbation December 31,1994 When I Was 29 Years Old", and then, "I Replaced It With Antique Shopping." Good for him. But I don't believe old teapots held back the tide for thirty years. He stopped, and then he had his Saturdays back and spent them on something he liked. A coach tells men in the trap that they are "substituting momentary pleasure for substantial and lifelong wins". He's right, and it shows that the habit was the substitute all along. One pastor says the real cure is "escaping into reality, into God Himself."

This is also how the old preacher from Chapter 20 squares with the rule against substitutes. His new affection isn't another small pleasure pushed into the gap. It's something big enough to live for. A young man who told his story on YouTube learned the same thing. He found he needed things to give his hours to, a purpose and work he cared about. Those are a life. A substitute is only a quieter way of feeding the same itch.

A psychiatrist who treats addiction says something that sounds like the opposite of this chapter: "You can pause something for a little while, but until you have a sustainable replacement, the behavior will just reemerge." Read him closely and he isn't recommending another hit. The replacement he means is a better way of meeting a bad feeling than hiding from it, and Chapter 5 was about exactly that. He also knows where the real thing is not to be had: "The internet can show us sexiness but cannot show love."

If you need a genuine break in your day, take one. You'll enjoy it more now that it doesn't have to end behind a locked door.

So you don't need a substitute. If an urge comes in the next few days, it's the Little Monster starving, and you can let that be your prop. Enjoy feeling him go.
